A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSA method and research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained content across layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical simulations in Section 5, benchmark experiments in Section 6, and audio classification and sensitivity results in Appendices B–E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds LiDAR retrieval, time-series classification, embedding analyses, and architecture controls in Appendices F–J.

M1.justification: The CCA projection, correlation-weighted cosine similarity, dimension truncation, and fitting/inference procedure remain unchanged. New experiments reuse CSA with different features or encoders. GPU and approximate-SVD acceleration are discussed as possibilities, without establishing an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Appendices F and G substantially extend the evaluated modalities and tasks: KITTI text-to-LiDAR place retrieval and handwritten-character classification using three-dimensional pen-motion time series paired with images or text. ImageNet, Leafy Spurge, Flickr30k, COSMOS, and MusicCaps coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Figure 11 adds a reported Lip-loc LiDAR-to-LiDAR retrieval reference, and Figure 13 adds comparisons using linear SVMs on CLIP and CSA embeddings. Comparators in the original experiments remain unchanged; extending ASIF to time-series classification alone does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: New protocols include KITTI's 5,000/6,000 train/test instances, 20-meter retrieval criterion and Recall@5, time-series one-vs-rest AUC, supervised linear probes, and ViT-L/14 architecture controls with different pretraining datasets. Table 1 also revises CLIP's reported pretraining size from 12B to 2B. Its Appendix A model identifier remains unchanged, so this revision does not establish rerunning the original experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained robustness and encoder-sensitivity studies, v3 adds detection-task sensitivity to s (Table 4), t-SNE analysis of 20 ImageNet classes (Figure 12), linear-SVM probes (Figure 13), and an architecture control (Figure 14). These substantially expand investigations of hyperparameter effects, embedding quality, and architectural explanations for performance.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the similarity-score distributions and Wilcoxon p-values in Figure 2. v3 introduces no additional repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error-bar reporting, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and plots are retained. New results include KITTI Recall@5 entries of 32.8 for CSA text queries and 32.4 for Lip-loc LiDAR queries, and time-series/image and time-series/text AUCs of 0.58 and 0.54 versus ASIF's 0.50 (Table 5). Table 4 and Figures 12–14 add sensitivity, clustering, probe, and architecture findings, including CLIP+SVM outperforming CSA+SVM at 35,000 training samples. These are additional evaluations under their respective settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, the linear data-generation assumptions, CCA derivation, distance bounds, and theoretical trade-off remain unchanged. The added appendix material supplies empirical analyses rather than new mathematical definitions, proofs, or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace 300,000-fold fewer paired data and sixfold fewer unimodal data with 50,000-fold fewer paired data for alignment given pretrained encoders. This qualifies the efficiency headline while retaining the central contributions. The conclusion replaces generic cross-modal retrieval with text-to-LiDAR, although its CLIP-comparison wording conflicts with Figure 11's Lip-loc reference.

C2.justification: v2's assertion that GPUs cannot accelerate CSA is replaced with discussion of possible GPU, randomized, and truncated-SVD acceleration. New analyses distinguish linear-probe evidence from cross-modal alignment and attribute gains to CSA after controlling architecture. The existing trade-off explanation and limitations concerning two modalities and encoder quality remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link and a reproducibility statement describing supplementary code, dataloaders, and execution resources. It also discloses NumPy implementation, 11% mislabeled training examples in the existing ImageNet detection experiments, and technical details for new experiments, including the LLaVA prompt, tsfresh features, and encoder configurations. Existing Appendix A hardware and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 retains its positioning relative to CLIP, CCA-based neural methods, and ASIF. Added references principally support new experiments and tools, including Lip-loc, tsfresh, DataComp, and t-SNE. Appendices F and G additionally claim priority for text-to-LiDAR retrieval and multimodal multivariate-time-series classification.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes comprise targeted abstract, contribution, limitation, and cross-reference edits; new reproducibility and acknowledgment sections; and additional appendix sections. Conference headers and heading typography also change, without a broad narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The appendix gains substantial visual evidence: a retrieval heatmap, embedding visualizations, linear-probe curves, and architecture-control plots in Figures 11–14, plus detection-sensitivity and time-series Tables 4–5. Existing figures are retained, with limited caption edits and relocation. Conference formatting also changes headings, headers, and page flow.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the empirical case by adding an architecture control absent from v2, broader modality tests, and embedding diagnostics. Code-access documentation and the qualified efficiency headline improve transparency. These gains are limited by sparse specifications for the new time-series and linear-probe experiments, while the conclusion introduces a misleading CLIP comparison for text-to-LiDAR results actually referenced against Lip-loc.
